sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: As the sun set that April evening, the wireless radio began to crackle.
sentences.zh: 那年四月的傍晚，随着太阳落山，无线电开始发出噼啪声。

sentences.en: It was a cold night in the North Atlantic, and ships were sending messages to their sisters.
sentences.zh: 北大西洋的夜晚寒气逼人，各艘船只都在向姐妹船发送消息。

sentences.en: Watch out, they said.
sentences.zh: 小心，它们说。

sentences.en: Icebergs ahead.
sentences.zh: 前方有冰山。

sentences.en: On board the RMS Titanic, a man named Jack Phillips was working at the wireless radio.
sentences.zh: 在泰坦尼克号上，一个叫杰克·菲利普斯的人正在无线电室工作。

sentences.en: He received word from another ship that pinpointed the location of heavy ice pack and a great number of bergs.
sentences.zh: 他从另一艘船那里收到了消息，明确指出了大片浮冰和大量冰山的位置。

sentences.en: Close to 11 p.m., another ship, the Californian, said it had come to a standstill in a dense field of ice.
sentences.zh: 晚上11点左右，另一艘船“加利福尼亚号”称，它被困在密集的冰区中，无法动弹。

sentences.en: Shut up.
sentences.zh: 闭嘴。

sentences.en: The wireless operator is supposed to have responded.
sentences.zh: 据称无线电操作员这样回应道。

sentences.en: I'm busy.
sentences.zh: 我很忙。

sentences.en: Busy with what?
sentences.zh: 忙什么？

sentences.en: Jack Phillips was sending and receiving personal messages over the wireless radio
sentences.zh: 杰克·菲利普斯当时正在通过无线电发送和接收私人信息，

sentences.en: for the ship's many wealthy and important passengers.
sentences.zh: 为船上许多富有且重要的乘客服务。

sentences.en: You know what happened next.
sentences.zh: 你知道接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: The Titanic struck an iceberg shortly afterwards.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，泰坦尼克号撞上了一座冰山。

sentences.en: It sank and killed more than 1,500 people on board.
sentences.zh: 它沉没了，船上1500多人丧生。

sentences.en: Today, we know there were many things that went wrong that night in 1912.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们知道1912年那个夜晚有很多环节出了错。

sentences.en: People mistakenly believed the Titanic was unsinkable.
sentences.zh: 人们错误地认为泰坦尼克号是永不沉没的。

sentences.en: There were not enough lifeboats to go around.
sentences.zh: 救生艇数量不足。

sentences.en: The lifeboats that did manage to get into the water eventually floated away with more than 400 empty seats.
sentences.zh: 最终成功下水的救生艇，上面竟有400多个空位。

sentences.en: But the story of what happened in the wireless room that night is less well-known.
sentences.zh: 但那天晚上无线电室里发生的故事却鲜为人知。

sentences.en: What might have happened if the wireless operator, the captain and crew,
sentences.zh: 如果无线电操作员、船长和船员，

sentences.en: had actually listened to the warnings that were coming in loud and clear?
sentences.zh: 真的听取了那些清晰响亮的警告，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Today on the show, we explore a great psychological mystery.
sentences.zh: 今天在节目中，我们将探讨一个伟大的心理学谜题。

sentences.en: We've all been provided with a plethora of ways to understand what other people are telling us.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都拥有多种多样的途径去理解他人所传达的信息。

sentences.en: Why do we so often fail to take heed?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们却常常置若罔闻？

sentences.en: The science of learning and the art of listening.
sentences.zh: 学习的科学与倾听的艺术。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: There are lots of reasons two people might misunderstand each other.
sentences.zh: 两个人之间产生误解的原因有很多。

sentences.en: But nearly all of them are either caused or compounded by a single factor.
sentences.zh: 但几乎所有原因都是由同一个因素引起或加剧的。

sentences.en: One or both parties has failed to hear what the other is actually saying.
sentences.zh: 其中一方或双方未能听清对方真正想表达的内容。

sentences.en: You see this in classrooms, in workplaces, in geopolitical settings.
sentences.zh: 你在教室、职场、地缘政治环境中都能看到这种情况。

sentences.en: It happens between strangers, between partners, between friends.
sentences.zh: 它发生在陌生人之间、伴侣之间、朋友之间。

sentences.en: At the University of Haifa in Israel, psychologist Guy Itzikoff studies the science of listening.
sentences.zh: 在以色列海法大学，心理学家盖伊·伊齐科夫专门研究倾听的科学。

sentences.en: Guy Itzikoff, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 盖伊·伊齐科夫，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Hi Shankar, great to be here.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔，很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Guy, I want to take you back to when you were 22 years old.
sentences.zh: 盖伊，我想带你回到你22岁的时候。

sentences.en: You once got into an argument with a very good friend.
sentences.zh: 你曾经和一位非常好的朋友吵过架。

sentences.en: Who was this friend, Guy?
sentences.zh: 这位朋友是谁，盖伊？

sentences.en: How long had you known him?
sentences.zh: 你们认识多久了？

sentences.en: Oh, I've known him since kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们从幼儿园就认识了。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is a long-standing friendship.
sentences.zh: 好的，看来这是一段长久的友谊。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: What caused the conflict?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了冲突？

sentences.en: It was a lot of time ago.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: I'm 38 now, so it seems like a different lifetime.
sentences.zh: 我现在38岁了，感觉像是上辈子的事。

sentences.en: But I wasn't invited to a social event that I really wanted to be invited to.
sentences.zh: 当时我没有被邀请参加一个我非常想去的社交活动。

sentences.en: Many of the popular kids were there.
sentences.zh: 很多受欢迎的孩子都在那里。

sentences.en: And I was never, not unpopular, but never in the popular group.
sentences.zh: 我从来不是，也不是不受欢迎，但从未进入过那个受欢迎的圈子。

sentences.en: And this friend was friends with some people in the popular group.
sentences.zh: 而这位朋友和那个圈子里的一些人是朋友。

sentences.en: And a couple of days after, I heard someone talking about this event.
sentences.zh: 几天后，我听到有人在谈论这个活动。

sentences.en: And it didn't really do anything to me until I heard this friend was there.
sentences.zh: 起初我没什么感觉，直到我听说这位朋友也在场。

sentences.en: That my friend was there.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友也在场。

sentences.en: And I thought that he did not tell me about this event, even though he was my best friend.
sentences.zh: 我心想，他竟然没告诉我这个活动，尽管他是我最好的朋友。

sentences.en: This is what I thought initially.
sentences.zh: 这是我最初的想法。

sentences.en: And I felt really, really insulted.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常、非常受侮辱。

sentences.en: Yeah, did you confront your friend or did you just simply stew in silence?
sentences.zh: 是吗，你是去质问他了，还是只是默默生闷气？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I played passive-aggressive for a while.
sentences.zh: 是的，我消极抵抗了一段时间。

sentences.en: So I said, okay, I'm going to play insulted.
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，好吧，我要装作很受伤的样子。

sentences.en: So I didn't answer his phone, his calls.
sentences.zh: 所以我没接他的电话。

sentences.en: And so I avoided him for a few days until we eventually met in an unplanned way for me.
sentences.zh: 我躲了他几天，直到我们后来意外地碰面了。

sentences.en: And what happened at this meeting?
sentences.zh: 那次见面发生了什么？

sentences.en: So he came to me and I was very cold.
sentences.zh: 他走过来找我，但我表现得很冷淡。

sentences.en: I wanted him to understand that I'm angry.
sentences.zh: 我想让他明白我很生气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And he was like, okay, so what's your problem?
sentences.zh: 他问我，好吧，你到底有什么问题？

sentences.en: Why are you being so distant and cold?
sentences.zh: 为什么表现得这么疏远和冷淡？

sentences.en: And what did I do to you?
sentences.zh: 我做什么对不起你的事了吗？

sentences.en: And then I vented about him not inviting me or not telling me about this event.
sentences.zh: 然后我就发泄了一通，抱怨他没邀请我或没告诉我那个活动。

sentences.en: I was like, how could he not invite me?
sentences.zh: 我说，他怎么能不邀请我？

sentences.en: Like, I always invite him to other events like this.
sentences.zh: 我总是邀请他参加类似的活动。

sentences.en: And when he gets the chance, he doesn't reciprocate.
sentences.zh: 可当他有机会时，却不回馈我。

sentences.en: And that he used this as an opportunity to be more in the popular group.
sentences.zh: 而且他利用这个机会去融入那个受欢迎的圈子。

sentences.en: And after so long, it's hard to remember the words, but I remember the feeling.
sentences.zh: 过了这么久，很难记起当时的原话，但我记得那种感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: You were hurt and you felt wounded and betrayed and you wanted him to understand how upset you were.
sentences.zh: 你感到受伤、委屈和被背叛，你想让他明白你有多难过。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I didn't even want an apology.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不需要道歉。

sentences.en: Like, I wanted to make him feel like I felt.
sentences.zh: 我只想让他感受到我的感受。

sentences.en: Did he try and explain what happened, Guy?
sentences.zh: 他有没有试图解释发生了什么，盖伊？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: So he was saying words in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 起初他在说话。

sentences.en: I had no idea what he said because I was too busy listening to myself.
sentences.zh: 但我根本不知道他在说什么，因为我忙着沉浸在自己的情绪里。

sentences.en: But when I get angry, I have a tendency to repeat the same thing over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我生气时，倾向于一遍又一遍地重复同样的话。

sentences.en: And after a few repetitions, I suddenly became aware that he's saying, you got it completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 重复了几次后，我突然意识到他在说，你完全搞错了。

sentences.en: I did call you.
sentences.zh: 我给你打过电话。

sentences.en: I did text you.
sentences.zh: 我给你发过短信。

sentences.en: And then I called him a liar.
sentences.zh: 然后我骂他是骗子。

sentences.en: But not only did you not invite me, but you also are lying to me.
sentences.zh: 不仅没邀请我，还在骗我。

sentences.en: The friend pulled out his phone and showed Guy the message he had sent, the call he had made.
sentences.zh: 朋友拿出手机，给盖伊看了他发的消息和拨打的通话记录。

sentences.en: And then Guy remembered.
sentences.zh: 然后盖伊想起来了。

sentences.en: He had recently switched phones because his battery had died.
sentences.zh: 他因为手机没电，最近刚换了手机。

sentences.en: His phone had been out of commission when his friend had tried to reach him.
sentences.zh: 他朋友联系他时，他的手机正好处于停用状态。

sentences.en: I felt so, so small.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常、非常渺小。

sentences.en: I felt like, wow, I completely misread the situation.
sentences.zh: 我心想，天哪，我完全误解了情况。

sentences.en: Like, I completely judged him without having, like, giving him the opportunity to explain it.
sentences.zh: 我竟然在没给他解释机会的情况下就完全评判了他。

sentences.en: And he was actually right.
sentences.zh: 他其实是对的。

sentences.en: And I felt really bad about it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 事后我感到非常内疚。

sentences.en: Some time later, after Guy became a psychologist, he got to experience what it felt like when the shoe was on the other foot.
sentences.zh: 后来，盖伊成为心理学家后，他亲身体验了角色互换的感觉。

sentences.en: He was working with a colleague in the field of education on a project.
sentences.zh: 当时他正与一位教育领域的同事合作一个项目。

sentences.en: His colleague decided to bring in a senior scholar from his field.
sentences.zh: 他的同事决定引入一位该领域的资深学者。

sentences.en: But when Guy and his colleague went to meet the other researcher, the senior scholar ignored him.
sentences.zh: 但当盖伊和同事去见那位研究员时，资深学者无视了他。

sentences.en: He had no interest in listening to Guy or hearing about what he might bring to the project.
sentences.zh: 他根本没兴趣听盖伊说话，也不想听盖伊能为项目带来什么。

sentences.en: My friend and I are about the same age.
sentences.zh: 我和我朋友年纪差不多。

sentences.en: His colleague is older than I, than both of us.
sentences.zh: 他的同事比我们俩都年长。

sentences.en: And, like, he looks, I felt like he's looking through me.
sentences.zh: 我感觉他好像透过我看向别处。

sentences.en: And he actually said, well, why do you need him for?
sentences.zh: 他甚至说，你们找他干什么？

sentences.en: Get someone from our own college.
sentences.zh: 从我们学院找个人不就行了。

sentences.en: And I felt so insulted.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常受辱。

sentences.en: Like, he literally said, looked at me and said, why do you need him for?
sentences.zh: 他真的看着我说，你们找他干什么？

sentences.en: Like, I don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 就好像我不存在一样。

sentences.en: Why do you need him for?
sentences.zh: 你们找他干什么？

sentences.en: And the truth is, I think, as human beings, we are incredibly sensitive to these markers of social rejection.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我认为作为人类，我们对这些社会排斥的信号极其敏感。

sentences.en: In fact, even with the first story you told me about the party, part of the reason you were angry was that you wanted to be part of this group and the group wasn't.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使是你刚才讲的那个派对的故事，你生气的部分原因也是你想成为那个群体的一员，但群体却没接纳你。

sentences.en: You felt that you weren't being welcomed into the group.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你没有受到群体的欢迎。

sentences.en: And in this case, you wanted to be part of this grand proposal and this person was rejecting you.
sentences.zh: 而在这次事件中，你想参与这个宏大的提案，而这个人却在拒绝你。

sentences.en: And as human beings, I think we're extraordinarily sensitive to any signal that someone actually might be dissing us, ignoring us, rejecting us.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我认为我们对任何暗示别人在轻视、忽视或拒绝我们的信号都异常敏感。

sentences.en: Of course, it's a basic human need.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一种基本的人类需求。

sentences.en: The need to belong.
sentences.zh: 归属感的需求。

sentences.en: The need to feel included and to be connected with other people.
sentences.zh: 被接纳并与他人建立联系的需求。

sentences.en: It goes with us through early childhood to our entire life.
sentences.zh: 这种需求伴随我们从童年早期到一生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, do you see examples of poor listening as you look around you, not just in your own life, Guy, but when you look at the media, on cable TV, faculty meetings,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你在生活中观察时，是否看到了很多倾听不佳的例子？不仅是在你自己的生活中，盖伊，当你观察媒体、有线电视、教职员会议、

sentences.en: cabinet meetings?
sentences.zh: 内阁会议时，

sentences.en: You know, do you see examples of poor listening everywhere you look?
sentences.zh: 你是否随处可见倾听不佳的例子？

sentences.en: Well, to remind you, I live in Israel, so I see more examples of poor listening than the other way around.
sentences.zh: 嗯，提醒你一下，我住在以色列，所以我看到的倾听不佳的例子比好的例子多得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: There is a sentence saying, to Israel is for opinions.
sentences.zh: 有一句话说，以色列人就是为了发表意见而生的。

sentences.en: So, unfortunately, I see poor listening everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以不幸的是，我随处可见倾听不佳的现象。

sentences.en: And even more, unfortunately, it seems to be escalating as time goes by.
sentences.zh: 更不幸的是，随着时间的推移，这种情况似乎还在升级。

sentences.en: Nowadays, with the televisions, at least in Israel, this is how I feel.
sentences.zh: 如今，至少在以色列的电视节目中，我是这种感觉。

sentences.en: So, the norm, unfortunately, became to bring someone and start arguing with them.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，现在的常态变成了请人来，然后开始和他们争吵。

sentences.en: So, if you don't argue with them, it's not interesting.
sentences.zh: 如果你不和他们争吵，那就没意思了。

sentences.en: It's all about the arguing and the yelling and who yells stronger and who dominates the conversation.
sentences.zh: 一切都是为了争吵、大喊大叫，看谁喊得更响，谁能主导对话。

sentences.en: And two people yell.
sentences.zh: 两个人都在大喊。

sentences.en: So, the one that you hear is the person who yells the loudeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你能听到的就是那个喊得最大声的人。

sentences.en: This is what I talk about, a toxic atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的有毒氛围。

sentences.en: It's always like, let's bring someone from the opposite that we disagree with and see and get them start yelling and then we'll respond.
sentences.zh: 总是这样：让我们请一个持相反意见的人来，让他们开始大喊大叫，然后我们再回应。

sentences.en: And as a listening researcher, this really, I get a bad feeling from listening to it.
sentences.zh: 作为一名倾听研究者，听到这些我真的感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: When we come back, how poor listening ruins conversations and undermines our relationships, and how to learn to listen better.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨倾听不佳如何破坏对话和人际关系，以及如何学会更好地倾听。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Now, good conversations might feel this way, but very often in our discussions with others, it can feel like we have two left feet.
sentences.zh: 好的对话可能感觉很顺畅，但我们与他人讨论时，往往感觉笨手笨脚。

sentences.en: At the University of Haifa, Guy Itzikoff studies the psychology of listening.
sentences.zh: 在海法大学，盖伊·伊齐科夫研究倾听的心理学。

sentences.en: He says that listening plays a bigger role in conversations than we imagine.
sentences.zh: 他说，倾听在对话中扮演的角色比我们想象的要重要得多。

sentences.en: Guy, it seems like listening should be the easiest thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 盖伊，听起来倾听应该是世界上最简单的事情了。

sentences.en: Someone speaks.
sentences.zh: 有人在说话。

sentences.en: All you have to do is sit there and pay attention.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的就是坐在那里，保持专注。

sentences.en: You say that one thing that makes it hard to do this well is that many of us are juggling a lot.
sentences.zh: 你说过，做好这件事的一个难点在于，我们许多人都忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: We suffer from a chronic lack of bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 我们正遭受着长期的带宽不足之苦。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Because listening is not that easy.
sentences.zh: 因为倾听并非那么简单。

sentences.en: Listening is costly.
sentences.zh: 倾听是有代价的。

sentences.en: It requires motivation.
sentences.zh: 它需要动力。

sentences.en: It requires cognitive ability.
sentences.zh: 它需要认知能力。

sentences.en: It requires time and effort.
sentences.zh: 它需要时间和精力。

sentences.en: And these are limited resources that we have.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是我们拥有的有限资源。

sentences.en: And we need to decide how to allocate them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要决定如何分配它们。

sentences.en: You know, like the famous sentence, time is money.

sentences.zh: 他们写了一篇简短的文章来论证自己的态度。

sentences.en: And then we told them that a few days later, they were going to be conversing with a listener.
sentences.zh: 然后我们告诉他们，几天后，他们将与一位倾听者进行交谈。

sentences.en: And so, for example, if you indicated that you were against vaccination cards, you will be paired with a listener who supposedly was in favor.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你表示反对疫苗接种卡，你会被分配给一位据称是支持该政策的倾听者。

sentences.en: And we had my research assistants in my lab.
sentences.zh: 我们实验室的研究助理参与了其中。

sentences.en: They go through 15 to 20 hours of listening training as they do both good listening condition and normal listening or what we call a moderate listening condition.
sentences.zh: 他们接受了15到20小时的倾听培训，因为他们既要进行良好的倾听，也要进行正常的倾听，或者我们称之为中等程度的倾听。

sentences.en: And so the speakers share their attitudes, either randomly assigned to either with a listener who exhibited good listening behavior, such as their reflection, question asking,
sentences.zh: 发言者分享他们的态度，被随机分配给表现出良好倾听行为的倾听者，例如复述、提问，

sentences.en: validation, which goes something like, thank you, Shankar, for sharing this with me.
sentences.zh: 以及认可，比如：“谢谢你，尚卡尔，愿意与我分享这些。”

sentences.en: I'm sure it wasn't easy for you.
sentences.zh: “我相信这对你来说并不容易。”

sentences.en: And the listeners reminded them that they held an opposite attitude.
sentences.zh: 倾听者提醒他们，自己持有相反的态度。

sentences.en: Guy and his colleagues found that the better the listener, the greater the sense of warmth speakers felt when talking to them.
sentences.zh: 盖伊和他的同事发现，倾听者表现得越好，发言者在交谈时感受到的温暖感就越强。

sentences.en: But that's not surprising.
sentences.zh: 但这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: What was surprising is that when paired with an excellent listener, speakers were more likely to moderate their views.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，当与优秀的倾听者交谈时，发言者更有可能缓和自己的观点。

sentences.en: They didn't shift their attitude, but they moved more towards the midpoint.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有改变立场，但他们的观点向中间靠拢了。

sentences.en: So they did move towards the listener's attitude, but they still kept their own valence or positivity or negativity.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实向倾听者的态度靠拢了，但仍保持着自己原有的倾向性，即积极或消极的立场。

sentences.en: Now, the most interesting thing was that we measured their attitude extremity, the extent to which their attitude is one-sided before the conversation and after.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，我们测量了他们态度的极端程度，即他们在对话前后态度片面化的程度。

sentences.en: And the change was significantly greater in the high-quality listening condition, meaning that their attitude became less one-sided.
sentences.zh: 在高水平倾听条件下，这种变化显著更大，意味着他们的态度变得不那么片面了。

sentences.en: And we replicated this finding across four experiments, different topics.
sentences.zh: 我们在四个不同的实验和不同的话题中重复了这一发现。

sentences.en: So this was a really interesting finding.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的发现。

sentences.en: You know, I'm thinking about that children's game that we all used to play, you know, where you have a rope and you're playing tug-of-war.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在想我们小时候常玩的那种游戏，就是拔河。

sentences.en: And, of course, you have these two sides lining up on opposite sides, and, you know, you want to dig your heels into the ground and pull on the rope as hard as you can.
sentences.zh: 当然，两队人马站在绳子的两端，你想扎稳脚跟，拼命拉绳子。

sentences.en: And you obviously want to pull in only one direction because, of course, if you give any ground, then the other side is going to win.
sentences.zh: 你显然只想往一个方向拉，因为如果你退让一步，对方就会赢。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, as a metaphor, you know, I'm wondering whether it fits the way many of us approach conversations,
sentences.zh: 作为一个隐喻，我在想这是否符合我们许多人处理对话的方式，

sentences.en: which is we are so intent on where that rope is that we actually feel like we have to pull really hard in only one direction.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们太执着于那根绳子，以至于觉得必须拼命往一个方向拉。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if we give any ground, then we're going to lose the battle altogether.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们退让，我们就会输掉整场战斗。

sentences.en: But really what you're saying is that when one side stops pulling, and in some ways there's no more tug-of-war to be played because, you know,
sentences.zh: 但你真正想说的是，当一方停止拉扯时，某种程度上拔河就不再存在了，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: the other side is not pulling in the opposite direction, you're now just holding the rope now.
sentences.zh: 另一方不再向相反方向拉扯，你现在只是握着绳子。

sentences.en: And now it allows you to basically say, where do I actually want to go with this rope?
sentences.zh: 这让你能够思考：我到底想带着这根绳子去哪里？

sentences.en: Do I want to go in this direction?
sentences.zh: 我想往这个方向走吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to go in the other direction?
sentences.zh: 我想往另一个方向走吗？

sentences.en: You become more self-reflective.
sentences.zh: 你变得更善于自我反思了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm actually saying that if you listen well, you will get a bigger rope.
sentences.zh: 是的，我实际上是说，如果你倾听得好，你会得到一根更大的绳子。

sentences.en: And there will be enough rope for both of you, and a mutual rope, because you will see, you will be better able to see the needs and interest of your conversation partner.
sentences.zh: 绳子对你们双方来说都足够了，这是一根共同的绳子，因为你会更好地看到谈话伙伴的需求和利益。

sentences.en: People often think that if they, they will be more effective if they dominate the conversation.
sentences.zh: 人们常认为，如果他们主导对话，效果会更好。

sentences.en: So whoever speaks louder in Israel, it's very true.
sentences.zh: 所以在以色列，谁说话声音大，这确实很普遍。

sentences.en: It's not true empirically, but it's true society-wise.
sentences.zh: 从经验上讲这不是真的，但在社会层面上确实如此。

sentences.en: If I speak louder, I'm dominating the conversation, and then I'm going to win.
sentences.zh: 如果我说话声音大，我就主导了对话，然后我就赢了。

sentences.en: And that's another misperception.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种误解。

sentences.en: But it's not easy to tell a person, you need to let go.
sentences.zh: 但要告诉一个人“你需要放手”并不容易。

sentences.en: And if you let go, and you really try to listen and understand your conversation partner, who you probably disagree with, it will be at your advantage, both of your advantages.
sentences.zh: 如果你放手，真正尝试去倾听和理解你的谈话伙伴——尽管你可能与他们意见不合——这对双方都有利。

sentences.en: But it's not an easy decision, because we're so used to try to dominate the conversation and afraid that if we won't dominate the conversation by speaking, we will lose.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一个容易的决定，因为我们太习惯于试图主导对话，并担心如果不通过说话来主导，我们就会输。

sentences.en: And then we end up by losing, both of us lose.
sentences.zh: 结果我们最终输了，双方都输了。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a great irony here, Guy, which is that very often when we find ourselves in disagreement with someone, we want them to basically say, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有一个巨大的讽刺，盖伊，那就是当我们发现自己与某人有分歧时，我们通常希望他们能说：

sentences.en: I'm open to new positions and new points of view.
sentences.zh: “我对新的立场和观点持开放态度。”

sentences.en: I'm willing to rethink my existing stance.
sentences.zh: “我愿意重新思考我现有的立场。”

sentences.en: And that's why we push so hard and we shout so loudly is we're trying to knock people off from their positions to take a more broad-based view of things.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们如此强硬、大声疾呼，我们试图把人们从他们的立场上拉下来，让他们采取更广泛的视角。

sentences.en: What you're finding in some ways is that it's actually not our arguments that have this effect on people, it's our listening that can have this effect on people.
sentences.zh: 你在某种程度上发现，实际上并不是我们的论点对人们产生了这种影响，而是我们的倾听产生了这种效果。

sentences.en: So it's a great paradox that, in fact, even if we were not focused on the quality of the relationship,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的悖论，事实上，即使我们并不关注关系的质量，

sentences.en: if we were just focused on our goals of actually trying to knock people off from that point of view,
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是专注于试图把人们从他们的观点上拉下来的目标，

sentences.en: we would be more effective if we actually did better listening and less arguing.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能更好地倾听、减少争论，效果会更好。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: So what I do with my students is I tell them a very simple task.
sentences.zh: 所以我给学生布置了一个非常简单的任务。

sentences.en: Your goal for the upcoming week is to learn something new about a colleague of yours.
sentences.zh: 你接下来一周的目标是了解你的一位同事的一些新情况。

sentences.en: One colleague each day.
sentences.zh: 每天了解一位同事。

sentences.en: After each conversation, you need to reflect on your listening.
sentences.zh: 每次谈话后，你需要反思自己的倾听过程。

sentences.en: What did you learn?
sentences.zh: 你学到了什么？

sentences.en: What prevented you from listening well?
sentences.zh: 是什么阻碍了你好好倾听？

sentences.en: What made you able to listen well?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你能够好好倾听？

sentences.en: How can you improve the next time?
sentences.zh: 下次你该如何改进？

sentences.en: So the gist is, even forget all the behaviors.
sentences.zh: 所以要点是，甚至可以忘记所有的技巧。

sentences.en: If you truly are interested in a person, you will be probably perceived as a good listener because you will do all these behaviors.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的对一个人感兴趣，你很可能会被视为一个好的倾听者，因为你会自然而然地表现出所有这些行为。

sentences.en: So like, think, for example, think of a person you love.
sentences.zh: 比如，想想你爱的人。

sentences.en: And this person comes and tells you, Shankar, I have something I want to share with you.
sentences.zh: 如果这个人走过来对你说：“尚卡尔，我有话想跟你说。”

sentences.en: You don't need me to tell you about what are the behaviors of good listening and the verbal and the nonverbal.
sentences.zh: 你不需要我告诉你什么是良好的倾听行为，什么是言语和非言语的技巧。

sentences.en: You're interested in this person and your behaviors will reflect this intereSt.
sentences.zh: 你对这个人感兴趣，你的行为就会反映出这种兴趣。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, is at the core.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是核心所在。

sentences.en: So now we can't be interested in every person.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不可能对每个人都感兴趣。

sentences.en: But I think the basic premise is if we adapt a mindset that every person can teach us something, every person knows something that we don't, every person has a story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为基本前提是，如果我们采取一种心态，即每个人都能教我们一些东西，每个人都知道一些我们不知道的事情，每个人都有一个故事。

sentences.en: If you're interested in this story, you will most likely be perceived as a good listener.
sentences.zh: 如果你对这个故事感兴趣，你很可能会被视为一个好的倾听者。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, I can imagine a situation where I'm speaking to somebody whom I like very much, where in a very calm setting, there are not a lot of distractions.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我可以想象一种情况，我正在和一个我很喜欢的人交谈，在一个非常安静的环境中，没有太多的干扰。

sentences.en: This person and I agree on a whole bunch of things.
sentences.zh: 我和这个人对很多事情都达成了一致。

sentences.en: They're talking.
sentences.zh: 他们在说话。

sentences.en: I find listening to be effortless and easy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得倾听毫不费力，非常轻松。

sentences.en: The conversation is great.
sentences.zh: 对话很棒。

sentences.en: Now, those situations do arise.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些情况确实会出现。

sentences.en: They happen with regularity, hopefully more often than not.
sentences.zh: 它们经常发生，希望发生的频率更高。

sentences.en: But really what we're called upon to do is situations that, in fact, don't meet all of those criteria.
sentences.zh: 但我们真正需要应对的是那些实际上并不符合所有这些标准的情况。

sentences.en: We have to actually talk to people whom we might not be close to.
sentences.zh: 我们必须与那些可能并不亲近的人交谈。

sentences.en: We might be talking to them in environments that are noisy or distracted.
sentences.zh: 我们可能在嘈杂或分心的环境中与他们交谈。

sentences.en: And we might, most importantly, be talking to people whom we disagree with.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我们可能正在与意见不合的人交谈。

sentences.en: And at some level,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，

sentences.en: I think what you're suggesting is that we have to bring to bear the same skills that we extend to the people we love and that we agree with to the people that we don't love and don't agree with if we're going to make any headway with them.
sentences.zh: 我想你建议的是，如果我们想与那些我们不爱、不同意的人取得任何进展，我们就必须运用我们对待所爱之人、所赞同之人时所用的同样技巧。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is why listening requires training.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么倾听需要训练。

sentences.en: Because for the people we love and are interested in, like you said, very easy.
sentences.zh: 因为对于我们爱和感兴趣的人，就像你说的，非常容易。

sentences.en: But the reality is that our life is filled with other people as well.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们的生活中也充满了其他人。

sentences.en: So this is why listening requires training and a decision to be a good listener.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么倾听需要训练，需要做一个好的倾听者的决心。

sentences.en: And it's really important, like we talked about being nonjudgmental towards the speaker.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要，就像我们谈到的要对发言者不带评判一样。

sentences.en: Also, it's really important to be nonjudgmental towards yourself when you realize that you might not be as good of a listener as you thought you are.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到自己可能不像想象中那么会倾听时，对自己不带评判也同样重要。

sentences.en: Most of us are not as good of a listener as we think we are.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人并不像自己认为的那样擅长倾听。

sentences.en: But even if you are a good listener, there are times when we cannot be.
sentences.zh: 但即使你是一个好的倾听者，也有无法做到的时候。

sentences.en: As we mentioned, listening is a resource that we don't always have.
sentences.zh: 正如我们提到的，倾听是一种我们并不总是拥有的资源。

sentences.en: You have talked about various techniques, and I know there's no sort of quick fix sort of guide to this,
sentences.zh: 你谈到了各种技巧，我知道这没有所谓的快速修复指南，

sentences.en: but I just want to talk about two or three important techniques that you and others have identified.
sentences.zh: 但我只想谈谈你和其他人确定的两三个重要技巧。

sentences.en: Can you just talk about this idea that good listening involves a variety of verbal and nonverbal cues?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个观点吗：良好的倾听涉及多种言语和非言语线索？

sentences.en: What do you mean by this idea?
sentences.zh: 你所说的这个想法是什么意思？

sentences.en: What are some of these cues, Guy?
sentences.zh: 盖伊，这些线索有哪些？

sentences.en: So nonverbal behaviors are, for example, our facial expressions.
sentences.zh: 非言语行为，例如我们的面部表情。

sentences.en: Nonverbal behaviors such as nodding, such as open body posture, eye contact is very important.
sentences.zh: 非言语行为，如点头、开放的身体姿势，眼神交流也非常重要。

sentences.en: And if the speaker sees that you are still paying attention to them, that you are still listening to them, you send them a meta message.
sentences.zh: 如果发言者看到你仍在关注他们，仍在倾听他们，你就向他们发送了一个元信息。

sentences.en: It's called a meta message, not a direct message, but that you are important.
sentences.zh: 这被称为元信息，不是直接信息，而是传达你很重要。

sentences.en: You are the focus of my attention.
sentences.zh: 你是我的关注焦点。

sentences.en: I want to understand you.
sentences.zh: 我想了解你。

sentences.en: And this message relaxes them.
sentences.zh: 这个信息让他们放松下来。

sentences.en: They feel important.
sentences.zh: 他们感到自己很重要。

sentences.en: They feel validated.
sentences.zh: 他们感到被认可。

sentences.en: Now, listening also has a verbal component, and this is something that is less known.
sentences.zh: 倾听也有言语成分，这是鲜为人知的。

sentences.en: No, because many think that listening is only silence.
sentences.zh: 因为许多人认为倾听只是沉默。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: For example, paraphrase.
sentences.zh: 例如，复述。

sentences.en: So when the speaker stops and doesn't have any more to add, or when you feel that you cannot encompass any more information,
sentences.zh: 所以当发言者停下来没有更多要补充时，或者当你觉得无法再容纳更多信息时，

sentences.en: it's really important to reflect or paraphrase or summarize in your own words, or if you can, the closest you can to the speaker's words.
sentences.zh: 用你自己的话，或者尽可能用接近发言者的话来反思、复述或总结是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And it's really important to ask afterwards, did I miss anything?
sentences.zh: 事后问一句“我漏掉了什么吗？”非常重要。

sentences.en: Would you like to add anything?
sentences.zh: “你还有什么想补充的吗？”

sentences.en: And this paraphrasing, we found, we find it in our experiment that is very powerful because it benefits both the listener and the speaker.
sentences.zh: 我们在实验中发现这种复述非常有效，因为它对倾听者和发言者都有益。

sentences.en: It benefits the listener because the speaker tells you about points that you missed.
sentences.zh: 它对倾听者有益，因为发言者会告诉你你漏掉的要点。

sentences.en: And there are studies showing that even good listeners remember up to 50% of the content.
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，即使是好的倾听者也只能记住高达50%的内容。

sentences.en: So it's, no one expects us to remember everything.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人指望我们记住一切。

sentences.en: So it helps the listener.
sentences.zh: 这确实有助于倾听者。

sentences.en: Most importantly, it helps the speaker to feel understood what people usually do and say,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，它帮助发言者感到被理解，而人们通常的做法和说法是，

sentences.en: yeah, Shankar, I understand you.
sentences.zh: “是的，尚卡尔，我理解你。”

sentences.en: That doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 那是不起作用的。

sentences.en: It's like me telling you, Shankar, trust me.
sentences.zh: 这就像我对你说：“尚卡尔，相信我。”

sentences.en: I can't tell you to trust me.
sentences.zh: 我无法要求你信任我。

sentences.en: I need to show you that you can trust me.
sentences.zh: 我需要向你证明你是可以信任我的。

sentences.en: So by reflection, I show you, I try to understand you.
sentences.zh: 所以通过反思，我向你展示，我试着去理解你。

sentences.en: Another one is asking good questions that benefit the speaker's needs and interests.
sentences.zh: 另一点是提出能满足说话者需求和兴趣的好问题。

sentences.en: Very, very important.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: Good questions can deepen the conversation and help speakers bring from within them insight that they didn't think that they about before.
sentences.zh: 好的问题可以深化对话，帮助说话者从内心深处挖掘出他们之前未曾意识到的见解。

sentences.en: Validation, which is not, yeah, Shankar, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 认可，这并不是说，是的，Shankar，我同意你的观点。

sentences.en: Validation is, especially in difficult conversation.
sentences.zh: 认可指的是，特别是在困难的对话中。

sentences.en: Thank you for sharing with me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你与我分享，Shankar。

sentences.en: I'm sure it wasn't easy for you.
sentences.zh: 我相信这对你来说并不容易。

sentences.en: So it validates the effort that the speaker's made and brings about closeness between the speaker and the listener.
sentences.zh: 所以这认可了说话者所付出的努力，并拉近了说话者与倾听者之间的距离。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, Guy, after doing all of this research and thinking, has it changed the way that you have tried to listen to other people?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，Guy，在做了所有这些研究和思考之后，这是否改变了你尝试倾听他人的方式？

sentences.en: Do you find yourself doing poor listening and telling yourself, here are the things that I can do?
sentences.zh: 你是否发现自己在倾听效果不佳时，会提醒自己：这些是我可以改进的地方？

sentences.en: Have you found yourself mid-conversation stopping yourself to try and practice what you preach?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾在对话中途停下来，试图实践你所宣扬的理念？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Last year in a class and there was a student who was very frustrated and she came to me at the end of the lesson and she complained about, you know,
sentences.zh: 去年在一堂课上，有一位学生非常沮丧，她在课后找到我，抱怨说，你知道的，

sentences.en: about the tasks and about how they don't have enough time.
sentences.zh: 关于作业，还有关于他们时间不够的问题。

sentences.en: Many students have a variety of complaints and I didn't, I didn't try to justify myself and I initially wanted to because I was tired.
sentences.zh: 很多学生都有各种各样的抱怨，我当时没有，我没有试图为自己辩解，虽然我起初想这样做，因为我当时很累。

sentences.en: It was a four hour course.
sentences.zh: 那是一门四个小时的课程。

sentences.en: And then I, I, I decided to practice what I preach and I did not defend myself.
sentences.zh: 然后我，我，我决定实践我所宣扬的，我没有为自己辩护。

sentences.en: But I, I, I asked follow-up questions.
sentences.zh: 但我，我，我问了后续的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I heard you're saying that this course is, you feel that even though I reduced the, the number of articles, this is still unfair.
sentences.zh: 所以我听到你说，你觉得这门课，即使我已经减少了文章的数量，这仍然是不公平的。

sentences.en: Why do you feel it?
sentences.zh: 为什么你会有这种感觉？

sentences.en: Do you have anything else?
sentences.zh: 还有别的事吗？

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, she shared with me that she was very frustrated because she had a, her boyfriend broke up with her and she was very angry.
sentences.zh: 最后，她告诉我，她非常沮丧，因为她有一个，她的男朋友和她分手了，她非常生气。

sentences.en: And she, she took it out on many people around her.
sentences.zh: 而她，她把气撒在了周围许多人身上。

sentences.en: She knew she was upset about the breakup with the boyfriend, but she was actually hurting a lot because she was extrapolating the anger to the people around her family,
sentences.zh: 她知道她是因为和男朋友分手而难过，但她实际上伤害了很多人，因为她把愤怒发泄到了周围的人、家人身上，

sentences.en: even like professors, university, friends.
sentences.zh: 甚至包括教授、大学、朋友。

sentences.en: And she told me like, after our conversation, it really helped me to relax, to unwind.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，在我们的谈话之后，这真的帮助我放松了下来，缓解了情绪。

sentences.en: And like, this made my day.
sentences.zh: 这让我的一天都变得美好了。

sentences.en: It's like, this made my day that I, I managed to really help her.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我真的成功帮助了她，这让我感到这一天很有意义。

sentences.en: And again, notice the power of listening.
sentences.zh: 再次注意倾听的力量。

sentences.en: It's, it's not easy.

sentences.zh: 每一天都是挑战，但我确实想相信我，我正在取得进步。
